title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. AI-generated video was used to depict a real person saying words she never said, and the output was published to a social platform under the poster's own account. The false statements were attributed to a named individual, which is what makes the material defamatory in form rather than merely synthetic.

The failure sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation. Nothing in the reporting indicates any check on whether the depicted statements were real before the videos were posted. Catching it would have required the poster to verify the claims against the person depicted, or a platform-level review of synthetic media depicting a named candidate. Neither is described as having happened.

What is established is that a cease-and-desist letter was sent, that it asserts the statements were never made, and that the campaign responded with another AI-assisted video. What is not established is whether any court has found defamation, whether any platform removed the videos, or what Van Orden's intent was. A cease-and-desist letter is an allegation, not a ruling.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI-generated deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden has posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including one shared on Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and accuses Van Orden of trying to fool voters and harm her reputation.

The letter warns that Van Orden could violate state defamation law and says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign called Cooke's action a tantrum. Cooke lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points. Van Orden responded to the letter with another AI-assisted video featuring a red duck saying "Cease and desist!"
